question: Who was responsible for the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
solution:
The correct answer is __**General Dyer.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Jallianwala Bagh massacre**, also known as the **Amritsar massacre**, took place on **13 April 1919**.
 
• During the annual** Baishakhi festival** in Amritsar, Punjab, British India, a sizable and nonviolent gathering had convened at the Jallianwala Bagh to express **disapproval of the Rowlatt Act** and the apprehension of pro-independence activists **Saifuddin Kitchlew** and **Satyapal**.
 
• Temporary **Brigadier General Reginald E. H. Dyer** encircled the mass of unarmed civilians and ordered open fire in reaction to their public gathering.
 
• After the incident, **Rabindranath Tagore renounced his 'Knighthood".**
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi **gave up his title of** 'Kaiser-i-Hind'** and **withdrew the Satyagrah against Rowlatt Act.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rowlatt Act**:

 
 
• The Rowlatt Act, also known as the** Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919**, was enacted by the British government, prompting the Rowlatt Satyagraha. 
 
• On the advice of the **Sir Sidney Rowlatt** who **chaired Sedition Committee**, this act was passed. Despite the Indian members' unanimous opposition, the Imperial Legislative Council rushed this act through **in March 1919.**
 
• It gave the government broad powers to stifle political activity and allowed the** two-year imprisonment of political prisoners without charge or trial.**
 
• Gandhiji demanded that the Rowlatt Act be opposed nationally.
